transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah, hi. Um… what brings me in is, I guess, this thing that happens when I think there might be a bat around—like at work, in the stockroom, if I hear something or see something flapping, or even just think it could be there. It’s immediate. Like, before I can even talk myself through it, my heart just jumps, I start sweating, and I get this really strong feeling like I have to get out right then. Not in a minute, not after I check—right then. It’s kind of embarrassing, honestly, but it feels really intense in the moment.
Do these episodes only happen when you think a bat might be around?

Yeah, pretty much—at least that’s when it really happens. It’s not like I’m walking around feeling that way all day. It’s specifically when I think there might be a bat nearby, or I see something kind of flapping, especially in the stockroom. The second that thought hits me—like, “what if that’s a bat?”—my body just reacts. My heart jumps, I start sweating, and I get this really strong need to get out right then. It’s very immediate.
When this happens, is your fear mainly that other people will notice you panicking or judge you?

I don’t think so… I mean, I do feel embarrassed after, or even kind of during it if someone’s right there, because I know it probably looks ridiculous for a grown man to react that way. But that’s not the main fear in the moment, if that makes sense.

When it hits, I’m not really thinking, “Oh no, people are judging me.” It’s more like everything narrows to, “I need to get away from this.” The embarrassment is kind of secondary—like something I think about once I’m already reacting or once it’s over. If nobody were around, I think I’d still have the same reaction.
Are you afraid of bats themselves?

Yeah… I guess I am. I mean, it’s not that I sit here logically thinking a bat in the store is definitely going to attack me or something. I know, in my head, that if there was a bat in the building, it probably isn’t trying to hurt me.

But if I see something that looks like one, or even just a quick flutter in the back hallway or the stockroom, it’s like my brain skips over all the reasonable stuff. It treats it like I’m in real danger right then. Like it’s not “maybe there’s a bat,” it feels more like “get away, now.” So… yeah, I’d say it’s the bat itself, or the possibility that it’s a bat, that sets it off.
Have you ever had one of these sudden panic-like episodes when there was no bat around and you weren’t thinking about bats?

No, not really. I mean, I’ve gotten stressed about other things like anybody, but those sudden episodes—the heart jumping, sweating, that feeling like I have to get out right now—those happen when I think there might be a bat, or something is flapping around and my mind goes there.

It’s especially in the stockroom or places like that where I feel like one could be hiding. If I’m just going about my day and I haven’t seen anything or I’m not thinking about bats, I don’t suddenly get hit with it out of nowhere. It’s really tied to that moment where I think, “Wait, is that a bat?” and then my body just reacts before I can calm myself down.
